findings.issue: The real-sudo acceptance test (SPEC-02) never checks that the EPERM -> `sudo -n kill` path actually ran. It only checks the outcome: two timeouts, a final error, and no leftovers. That outcome is also reached when sudo itself kills the whole command. So the test can pass on Ubuntu 24.04 without testing the fix at all, and it does not check the design's key assumption (the root orphan stays in the attempt's process group).
findings.evidence: Builder's concern: sudo >= 1.9.14 with `Defaults use_pty` (Ubuntu 24.04 sudoers) runs the command under a root monitor in a new session/process group, and that monitor relays signals to the command's whole process group. In that mode, retry's SIGTERM reaches the sudo front end, the monitor sends SIGTERM to the group with sh+flock+sleep, and all of them die. Attempt 2 then gets the lock and every assertion at lines 211-216 passes. It would pass equally on the pre-change retry.js, so the spec's claim that it fails before the change is not guaranteed. In the same mode, a real apt-get that ignores or outlives SIGTERM sits outside pgid P: `sudo -n kill -- -P` misses it, `groupExists(P)` returns false (ESRCH), and reap reports success while the lock is still held. That is the run #68 failure again, and this test cannot show it. In non-pty mode the test does exercise the fallback. Which mode the runner uses is decided only by the environment, and nothing in the test records it.
findings.fix: Add an assertion that the fallback was used, e.g. `expect(stdout).toMatch(/retry: could not send SIG(TERM|KILL) to process group \d+ \(EPERM\)/)` and `expect(stdout).toMatch(/retry: sent SIGKILL to process group \d+ with sudo/)`. If CI then fails because sudo runs under use_pty, the spec's assumption ('the orphan stays in the attempt's group', Not doing: /proc walk) is shown to be wrong and must go back to spec. Do not let it pass silently. Optional: on failure, log `ps -o pid,pgid,sid,ruid,args` for the marker so the CI log shows the group layout. The file is locked, so the orchestrator must allow this change.

findings.issue: With the script `flock -n "$1" sleep "$2"; true`, a held lock makes `flock -n` fail, after which `true` runs and sh exits 0. Attempt 2 then logs `succeeded` and the helper exits 0. The text `failed with exit code` can never appear, so this assertion is dead. The spec's parenthetical about the pre-change failure ("fails with exit code 1") is wrong for the same reason. The test still fails before the change, through the warning count (1, not 2) and the exit code (0, not 1).
findings.evidence: `; true` at line 206 hides flock's exit status.
findings.fix: Replace the assertion with `expect(stdout).not.toContain('succeeded')`, or make a lock failure visible (e.g. `flock -n "$1" sleep "$2" || exit 7; true`) and keep the `failed with exit code` check.

findings.issue: If the child exits while the kill timer's `reap` is running, `finish` starts a second `reap` loop on the same group. On every poll both loops send SIGKILL, and with EPERM both run sudo, so sudo calls and log lines double for up to 2 s. Settling is still correct because of the `settled` guard.
findings.evidence: killTimer callback awaits reap(pid) at line 141. finish (line 153) calls reap(pid) without checking whether one is already running. clearTimeout(killTimer) has no effect on a timer that has already fired.
findings.fix: Keep the reap promise in a variable and reuse it: `reaping ??= reap(pid, sudoKill)` in both places.

findings.issue: The test gets the child's pid only from the fake sudo. If a regression means sudo is never called, `pid` stays undefined, and the `finally` cleanup's `killGroup(undefined)` leaves the hanging `setInterval` child running after the test run. SPEC-04's cleanup (line 145) has the same problem.
findings.fix: Get the pid from a spy on `child_process.spawn`, or from the `retry: ... attempt 1` / process-group log line, so cleanup works even when sudo is never called.

findings.issue: SPEC-04 says the fake sudo's first call is `(<pid>, 'SIGTERM')`. The test checks only the signal, not the pid.
findings.fix: Also check `typeof calls[0][0] === 'number'` and that it is > 0, or compare it to the pid the spawn spy got.

summary: All 8 SPEC items are implemented as the spec describes. retry.js gets killGroup outcomes, groupExists, sudoKillGroup, a bounded reap after every attempt (2 s, 250 ms polls) and the stuck -> ::error:: exit 1 path. runProcessGroup replaces spawnSync in the speed-limits test, and both Linux-CI sudo tests clean up in try/finally. Gates pass: tests, lint and typecheck. Line count is 490 against a budget of 330 (the gate warns; mostly test code). Locally, the targeted tests pass (17 passed, 2 Linux-only skipped), the spec's Run command behaves as described (about 2 s, exit 1), and no processes were left behind. One MAJOR finding, about the builder's use_pty concern: the real-sudo test SPEC-02 checks only the outcome, never that the EPERM -> sudo fallback ran. Under sudo use_pty, sudo's own monitor kills the command's whole group, so SPEC-02 would pass even on the old code, and a real apt orphan outside the attempt's group would go undetected. Asserting the `with sudo` log line makes CI either confirm or disprove the design's process-group assumption. Minor findings: a dead `failed with exit code` assertion (`; true` turns a held lock into exit 0), and reap loops that can run twice at once.
